reviews.rationale: Selected SEC rows show sequential GAAP revenue growth led by the financial technology solutions component, with subscription services also higher and hardware and professional services lower. Gross profit rose while total costs of revenue and total operating expenses also rose, so operating income improved only modestly and the incremental revenue did not translate proportionally into operating profit. The larger pretax and net income improvement is not attributable to operations alone: the warrant fair value line moved from a negative to a positive contribution and interest income net also increased, so a meaningful part of the bottom-line step-up reflects non-operating items whose persistence is unknown. The income tax line moved from a benefit to a small expense, which is a larger tax drag rather than a smaller one, and it partly offsets the pretax improvement. Company-reported gross payment volume rose, but it is an operating metric on a different basis from revenue and cannot be treated as revenue or as a causal driver. All comparisons are sequential displayed-value arithmetic between two selected quarters, not year-over-year, not guidance versus realized results, and not a complete filing; no non-GAAP measures, guidance, segment economics, or management explanation are in this extract. Because the operating versus non-operating split of the profit improvement is unresolved and the thesis carries no assumptions, catalysts, or invalidation conditions to test against, the research state is held for review rather than advanced.
